thread.title_full: MSU Extension to host webinars on short-term rental policy options for local officials

author: Great Lakes Wire
title: MSU Extension to host webinars on short-term rental policy options for local officials
text:
Michigan State University Extension announced on April 15 that it will hold two webinars in 2026 aimed at helping local government officials understand their policy options for short-term rentals. The “Short-Term Rental Policy Options for Local Communities” programs will take place on May 20 and October 6, each running from 6:30 to 8 p.m. Eastern Time.
The webinars are designed to address the growing presence of short-term rentals (STRs) across Michigan and provide guidance for communities reviewing their plans and policies. According to MSU Extension, the sessions will cover trends and research related to STRs, sources of data for examining local situations, an overview of regulatory tools, enforcement strategies, key court cases, and examples from Michigan communities.
Registration is now open at events.anr.msu.edu/STR26. The cost is $25 per person or $20 for Master Citizen Planners. All registrants will receive a recording of the program.
In the previous year, MSU Extension reported that 116 local leaders participated in similar programs. Evaluations indicated that most participants found the content valuable; nine out of ten respondents said they felt able to suggest ways to regulate or enforce STRs in their communities after attending. One participant commented they were ready to “assist my Planning Board with their development of a viable STR section to the ordinance,” while another planned to “negotiate a reasonable STR ordinance” locally.
A report by the MSU Extension Center for Local Government Finance and Policy highlighted that STRs have been expanding statewide and may impact local housing markets while also filling gaps in visitor accommodations.
The College of Agriculture and Natural Resources at Michigan State University addresses challenges in food, health, and environment through education and outreach according to its official website . The college extends its presence across Michigan through research centers and extension services according to its official website . In fall 2021, it reported an enrollment of 3,735 students with more than 340 scientists engaged in research according to its official website . The college focuses on fostering a healthy world through student preparation, knowledge dissemination, sustainable agriculture practices according to its official website , collaborates through major research centers and engages participants via MSU Extension according to its official website .
